*"Recipe: Crispy Veg Cutlets"* *_Ingredients:-_* *For the Vegetable Mixture:* * Boiled Potatoes: 4 medium (peeled and mashed) * Paneer: ½ cup (grated) * Carrots: ½ cup (grated) * Capsicum: ¼ cup (finely chopped) * Onion: ¼ cup (finely chopped) * Green Chilies: 1 tbsp (finely chopped) * Coriander Leaves: ¼ cup (finely chopped) * Chili Flakes: 1 tsp * Mixed Herbs / Oregano: 1 tsp * Black Pepper Powder: 1/3 tsp * Lemon Juice: 1 tbsp (can substitute with Amchur or Chaat Masala) * Salt: To taste * (Optional: You can also add finely chopped cabbage, beans, or spinach) *For the Slurry (Coating):* * Corn Flour: 4 tbsp * All-Purpose Flour (Maida): 4 tbsp * Black Pepper Powder: A pinch * Salt: A pinch * Water: As needed to make a thick batter *For the Outer Layer:* * Bread Crumbs: As required * Oil: For deep frying *_Instructions:-_* *1. Prepare the Vegetable Base* In a large mixing bowl, combine the mashed potatoes, grated paneer, carrots, capsicum, onions, green chilies, and coriander leaves. Add the chili flakes, mixed herbs, black pepper powder, salt, and lemon juice. Mix everything thoroughly by hand, ensuring the potatoes are well mashed and the spices are evenly distributed. *2. Shape the Cutlets* Clean your hands and take a small portion of the mixture. Roll it between your palms and shape it as desired. You can make them oval, egg-shaped, or the traditional round flat shape. Repeat until all the mixture is used. *3. Prepare the Coating Slurry* In a separate bowl, mix equal parts corn flour and maida (4 tbsp each). Add a pinch of salt and pepper. Gradually add water and whisk until you achieve a smooth, thick batter. Ensure it is not too thin. *4. Coat the Cutlets* Place the bread crumbs in a plate. Take a shaped cutlet and dip it into the flour slurry using a fork (this helps drain the excess batter). Immediately place it onto the bread crumbs and coat it evenly on all sides, tapping gently to ensure the crumbs stick. * Pro Tip: For extra crispiness and to prevent the cutlet from breaking in oil, you can do a "Double Coating" by dipping the bread-crumbed cutlet back into the slurry and then into the bread crumbs a second time. *5. Fry the Cutlets* Heat oil in a pan on medium to medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, carefully place the cutlets in the pan. Avoid low heat as it will make the cutlets soggy; high heat ensures they turn crispy. Fry until they reach a dark golden brown color, flipping them occasionally to ensure even cooking. *6. Serving* Remove the cutlets and place them on a kitchen paper towel to drain any excess oil. Serve these hot and crispy veg cutlets with tomato ketchup or green chutney. Note: You can store these prepared, uncooked cutlets in an airtight container in the freezer. When ready to eat, take them out an hour before and deep fry or air fry them directly.
